subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should shared-workspace memory-core dreaming enforce agent isolation by default, or is a configurable dreaming.agents allowlist an acceptable supported boundary?
rationale: Current docs promise isolated multi-agent state while runtime pools shared-workspace dreaming material; the fix changes a security-sensitive memory boundary and may add public config/API surface.

options.title: Enforce Default Agent Isolation
options.body: Dreaming should process the current agent's sessions and corpus by default, with any cross-agent sharing requiring an explicit opt-in contract.

options.title: Accept Configurable Allowlist
options.body: Land the narrower dreaming.agents allowlist as the supported operator-controlled isolation mechanism and document that unset still sweeps all configured workspaces.

options.title: Document Workspace Pooling As Expected
options.body: Keep workspace-level pooling but update docs and warnings to say multi-agent dreaming isolation requires separate workspaces or separate gateways.

recommendation.title: Enforce Default Agent Isolation
recommendation.body: Dreaming should process the current agent's sessions and corpus by default, with any cross-agent sharing requiring an explicit opt-in contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the current assignee and already narrowed the issue to the shared-workspace isolation boundary in the discussion.
